title: Isaiah (Part 1)
hook: Isaiah begins his book with a single strange word—chazon, "vision"—and everything that follows depends on it. He is not reporting rumors or offering opinions; he has seen something, the way a person standing in the temple sees rather than merely hears the covenant enacted around them. That distinction matters most in chapter 6, where Isaiah's own vision opens "in the year that king Uzziah died," the very moment Judah's earthly security collapsed into grief and uncertainty. Into that vacuum comes the sight of the Lord "high and lifted up," a throne-room encounter so overwhelming that Isaiah cries out for his own unclean lips before he can utter a word of prophecy to anyone else. Between the funeral lament of "How is the faithful city become an harlot!" and the tender, betrayed love song of the vineyard in chapter 5, these opening chapters trace the ache of a covenant relationship gone wrong—and the terrifying, merciful vision of a God still willing to purify and send. Sit with Isaiah's eyes this week, and you may find your own vision opened too.
